name: Grata (acquired by Datasite, June 2025)
hq_country: USA (New York); parent Datasite is USA (Minneapolis), owned by CapVest. Grata offices: New York, London, Paris, Frankfurt, Sydney.
data_types: Private-company fundamentals (verified financials/revenue estimates, employee counts, ownership structures incl. PE-backed flags), 10M+ executive contacts, business locations, 200K+ conference/trade-show attendee and sponsor lists, growth signals, comp sets, and 1M+ financial transaction records (M&A/funding deal history) per the Datasite product page. 150+ data points, ~70+ fields per company. No advertised acquisition-likelihood/propensity score.
coverage_geo: 21M-22M+ global private and public companies (figure varies 19M/21M/22M across Grata and Datasite pages). Countries explicitly named: North America (US/Canada), UK, France, Germany, Australia. Datasite's May 2026 acquisition of Valu8 extends European coverage to ~70M companies. NO Asia or Japan coverage is claimed anywhere in Grata/Datasite public materials; the 2024-25 international expansion announcement lists only UK, France, Germany, Australia and says further expansion is 'in the future'. This is the single biggest gap for an Asia-focused buyer.
history_depth: Not disclosed. 1M+ financial transactions are claimed but no start year is published. Unknown.
api: Yes. Full API with four documented endpoint families: Search API (thesis-based keyword search), Similar API (look-alike companies from a domain list), Enrichment API (firmographic append), and List API. Docs at https://docs.grata.com/ (Stoplight-hosted; the public landing page renders no schema without JS, so REST-vs-GraphQL was not verifiable — Inference: REST, based on the endpoint naming convention).
bulk_delivery: Yes. A 'Data Warehouse' option delivers the full underlying dataset via SFTP or Snowflake, refreshed weekly, covering private-company fundamentals, executive contacts, employee details, business locations and conference data (per businessbrokerfinder.us.com review, 2026). Platform data itself is refreshed daily.
pricing: Mostly quote-only; annual commitment, per-seat, no monthly option. One public list price point: Capterra lists Grata starting at USD 15,000/year, flat rate, single plan, free trial available (source: https://www.capterra.com/p/193002/Product-Search/pricing/, observed 2026). Third-party aggregator costbench.com cites a median of ~USD 155,000/yr from 6 verified purchases and ~USD 7,200+/seat/yr — flag: costbench is an unverified aggregator of uncertain methodology, treat as a weak third-party estimate, not a price. Data Warehouse / API add-on pricing is not published anywhere.
ml_training_license: Unknown. No public terms addressing AI/ML training were located. Inference: the Data Warehouse (SFTP/Snowflake) product is the delivery mode most likely to come with negotiable training rights, since it is explicitly sold as a full dataset license — but this must be confirmed in writing with Datasite.
language: English (platform, data labels and docs).
update_frequency: Platform data refreshed daily; Data Warehouse bulk feed refreshed weekly. Vendor claims 99%+ accuracy based on weekly external audits.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Data-model fit is strong — verified financials, ownership, headcount, growth signals and 1M+ transaction records delivered as a weekly bulk feed to Snowflake is close to an ideal training substrate. But coverage is North America / Western Europe / Australia only, with no Japan or Asia data, which makes it a poor primary source for a Japan-focused M&A advisory firm. Best considered as a source of cross-border buyer-side data or as label data for training on Western deal outcomes.
budget_tier: mid ($10k-50k/yr) for a small platform seat count based on the Capterra USD 15,000 starting figure; likely enterprise (>$50k/yr) once the API and Data Warehouse dataset licence are added — Inference, since neither add-on is publicly priced.

name: Sourcescrub
data_types: Bootstrapped/founder-owned private-company profiles built from 220K+ scraped sources, including 190K+ scrubbed conference and trade-show exhibitor lists (its signature dataset), revenue and headcount estimates, growth/trend signals, ownership and investment-activity tracking, and configurable scoring ('1 Score / N Rules' per tier — a user-defined lead score, not a vendor M&A propensity model). M&A transaction history is not marketed as a headline dataset.
coverage_geo: 14M-16M+ private companies (14M cited on a competitor-comparison page, 16M on the pricing page) and 220K sources / 115K-190K conference lists. Core sourcing is US and UK private-company filings, trade data and proprietary intelligence. Asia/Japan: no coverage figures published. A competitor (Amafi.ai) states Sourcescrub has 'limited integration with Tokyo Commercial Research [Tokyo Shoko Research], Teikoku Databank, or local FSA filings' and that APAC coverage is 'materially weaker' — flag: this is a competitor's marketing blog, not a vendor statement, and should be verified directly, though it is directionally consistent with Sourcescrub's stated US/UK sourcing.
history_depth: Not disclosed. Unknown.
api: Partial — API is not in the standard tiers. It is sold as a separate add-on called 'Data Connect (Cloud & API)', described as 'tailored data integration solutions', priced on request. No public developer documentation was found (the apitracker.io profile for Sourcescrub has all technical fields empty: no API type, no docs URL, no auth, no endpoints). Also integrates with Salesforce, Sugar CRM, DealCloud and Affinity.
bulk_delivery: Yes, implied — the 'Data Connect (Cloud & API)' add-on names a cloud/warehouse delivery path alongside the API, but no formats, cadence or schema are published. Unknown in detail.
pricing: Quote only. All three tiers — Essentials (1 Score / 5 Rules), Plus (1 Score / 15 Rules, 250 companies), Professional (1 Score / unlimited Rules, 1,000 companies) — show 'Request pricing' with no amounts or currency on the official pricing page (observed 2026). The Data Connect API add-on is likewise priced on request. Third-party sites (Capterra, GetApp, SoftwareAdvice, research.com) also list no public price. Vendor-adjacent commentary indicates price scales with AUM/deal volume, user count, export limits, CRM integrations and custom-research requirements.
ml_training_license: Unknown. No public terms addressing AI/ML training were located.
language: English.
update_frequency: Not disclosed. Unknown.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The conference/exhibitor-list dataset is a genuinely differentiated signal for finding founder-owned companies, and growth/headcount estimates are usable features. However, M&A deal-event history is not a headline dataset, API access is an unpriced bespoke add-on with no public docs, and Asia/Japan depth appears weak — so it is a poor primary training source for a Japan-focused model. Weak-to-moderate fit.
budget_tier: unknown — no public price point exists at any tier, and the API/bulk add-on is separately negotiated.

name: Cyndx (Finder / Owner / Raiser / Scholar / Valer)
data_types: Company and investor database with AI semantic search over what companies actually do (rather than SIC/NAICS codes); comparable-transaction and valuation analysis (Valer); capitalisation-table management (Owner); capital-raise counterparty matching (Raiser); AI-generated 15-20 page research reports (Scholar). Most relevant here: a genuine predictive score — 'Projected to Raise' (P2R), which forecasts a company's need to raise capital up to six months ahead, with vendor-claimed accuracy of 79% globally and 86%+ in the US. Note P2R predicts FUNDRAISING, not acquisition; Cyndx does not publicly market an acquisition-likelihood score.
coverage_geo: 32M+ private and public companies and investors (current figure on cyndx.com/products; a 2022 Middle Market Growth interview cited 16.5M, so the database has roughly doubled). Global. Notably, Cyndx supports translation across seven languages INCLUDING JAPANESE (French, German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish) to ingest and search non-English company information — one of the few Western deal-sourcing platforms to name Japanese explicitly. No Japan-specific company or deal counts are published.
history_depth: Not disclosed. Unknown.
api: Unknown / not publicly documented. No developer portal, API documentation or endpoint reference was found on cyndx.com, softwaresuggest, or in press coverage. Cyndx's own site and product pages returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching, so this could not be exhaustively verified. Inference: Cyndx is sold as a seat-based SaaS platform, with programmatic access (if any) available only by negotiation.
bulk_delivery: Unknown / not publicly documented.
pricing: Quote only. No amounts, currency or plan names are published on cyndx.com or on aggregators (softwaresuggest.com/cyndx shows only a 'request a quote' form; observed 2026). Vendor states it is 'trusted by 100+ world-class organizations', implying an institutional per-seat model.
ml_training_license: Unknown. No public terms addressing AI/ML training were located.
language: English platform; ingests and translates 7 languages including Japanese.
update_frequency: Not disclosed. Unknown.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Conceptually the closest of the deal-sourcing platforms to what is wanted — it already ships a production predictive model (P2R) over a 32M-company graph and explicitly handles Japanese-language source material. But the prediction target is a capital raise rather than an M&A exit, and with no documented API, no bulk delivery and no published pricing, it looks like a tool to buy rather than a dataset to train on. Moderate fit; worth a sales call specifically to ask whether raw/scored data can be licensed.

name: Inven.ai
data_types: AI-classified private-company profiles built by reading company websites across languages (rather than relying on industry codes or self-reported categories); company basics, ownership structures, financial data with links to underlying public filings (notably strong on European private financials), 3M+ transactions (M&A/deal records), 430M+ verified executive/professional contacts, and market/competitor analysis. No advertised acquisition-propensity score.
coverage_geo: 28M+ private companies across 160+ markets, spanning North America, Europe, LATAM and APAC (APAC is named as a covered region on comparison pages, but the homepage gives no Asia or Japan breakdown and Japan is not specifically called out anywhere found). Vendor claims 16M more companies than PitchBook and 93% search accuracy. Inference: the website-reading classification approach is genuinely language-agnostic and could work well on Japanese-language company sites, but Japan depth is unverified.
history_depth: Not disclosed. Unknown.
api: Partial. No public REST API documentation was found (www.inven.ai/pricing and /mcp both returned HTTP 404). The homepage references an 'Inven MCP for Private Market Company Data' — a Model Context Protocol server for programmatic/LLM access — and an 'Integrations' menu exists, but no endpoint reference, auth scheme or docs URL was reachable. An MCP server is a query interface, not a bulk-extraction channel, so it is unlikely to support training-scale data pulls.
bulk_delivery: Unknown / not publicly documented.
pricing: Mixed and unverified. Capterra lists Inven as 'Contact vendor for pricing' with a free trial and no free version, and no starting price (source: https://www.capterra.com/p/10005965/Inven/, observed 2026). Third-party comparison pages cite USD 10,000 per user/year, and one cites a 'Professional plan at USD 99/month' — flag: neither figure was confirmed on any Inven-owned page (Inven's own pricing URL 404s), and the two figures are inconsistent with each other, so treat both as unverified third-party estimates and not prices.
ml_training_license: Unknown. No public terms addressing AI/ML training were located.
language: English platform; AI explicitly reads company websites 'across languages', which is the mechanism by which non-English markets are covered.
update_frequency: Not disclosed. Unknown.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The language-agnostic website-classification approach plus 3M+ transaction records and 28M companies is attractive, and Inven is one of the few vendors in this group whose sourcing method should generalise to Japanese-language company data. But with no reachable API docs, no bulk-delivery product, no confirmed pricing and no published Japan coverage figures, it cannot be assessed as a training-data source without a direct vendor conversation. Moderate potential, low verifiability.
budget_tier: mid ($10k-50k/yr) — Inference from the unverified USD 10,000/user/yr third-party figure; Inven publishes no price of its own.

name: Axial
data_types: A members-only deal network / marketplace rather than a licensable dataset: sell-side engagements posted by lower-middle-market investment banks and business brokers, matched to buyer profiles (PE funds, family offices, strategics, search funds). Axial also publishes league tables and periodic deal-activity reports. Inference: the platform's value is live proprietary deal flow and counterparty matching, not a structured historical M&A transaction database available for extraction.
coverage_geo: United States-focused lower middle market (broadly companies with roughly USD 5M-250M enterprise value, per Axial's general market positioning). No Asia or Japan coverage. Note: axial.net, /pricing, /forum and /about-us all returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching, and the Capterra and G2 listings returned 404/403, so coverage figures could not be verified from primary sources in this session.
history_depth: Not verified. Unknown.
api: Unknown / not publicly documented. No developer portal or API documentation was located, and primary pages were unreachable (403). Inference: no data API — Axial is a web marketplace, and its deal information is confidential to matched counterparties by design.
bulk_delivery: No / not offered. Inference: a members-only marketplace of live confidential sell-side mandates is structurally incompatible with bulk data licensing.
pricing: Not verified in this session — quote only as far as could be established. Axial's own pricing page returned HTTP 403 and the Capterra/G2 listings were unreachable, so no price point is reported here. Historically Axial has operated a tiered annual membership for buy-side members and a separate model for sell-side advisors, but no amount is being asserted because none could be sourced. Treat as unknown pending a direct check of https://www.axial.net/pricing/ from a browser.
ml_training_license: Unknown, but Inference: almost certainly not permitted — deal information on Axial is confidential to matched parties and members agree to confidentiality as a condition of access, which is fundamentally inconsistent with extracting it for model training.
language: English.
update_frequency: Continuous (live marketplace postings). Inference.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Poor fit as a training-data source. It is a US-only origination channel for live confidential mandates, with no API, no bulk delivery and confidentiality terms that would preclude ML use. It may have standalone value to JCAI as a cross-border buyer-side origination channel for US targets, but that is a business-development decision, not a data purchase.

name: Preqin (a BlackRock company)
hq_country: United Kingdom (London); wholly-owned subsidiary of BlackRock (USA) since the acquisition closed March 2025
data_types: Private capital fund performance; PE, VC, real estate, infrastructure, natural resources and hedge fund data; deals and exits including M&A; secondaries; fundraising; LP and GP profiles; private-company financials; service-provider data.
coverage_geo: Global. Publicly stated scale: 235,000+ funds and 67,000+ companies/investors (Feeds API page); older figures cite 190,000 funds, 60,000 fund managers, 30,000 institutional investors. Research staff across US, Europe and Asia offices, but no Japan- or Asia-specific company or deal count is published. Inference: Asia/Japan depth is likely thinner than US/Europe given the research-office model and the PE/VC (rather than broad company-registry) focus.
history_depth: Founded 2003 as Private Equity Intelligence; roughly 20+ years of fund-performance history. Per-dataset (e.g. deal-level) historical depth is not publicly itemised.
api: Yes — two products: the Preqin API for application-level access, and the Feeds API for bulk data feeds. REST-based, OAuth2 or Basic (username/API key) auth, CSV bulk delivery, daily sync. Marketing page: https://www.preqin.com/our-products/feeds-api. Deeper technical docs sit behind a client portal (docs.preqin.com) that is not publicly browsable.
bulk_delivery: Yes — the Feeds API delivers full and incremental dataset dumps as CSV files on a scheduled (daily) basis.
pricing: No public list price; Preqin does not publish rates and requires sales contact. Third-party estimates only (all labelled as third-party estimates, observed 2026): Vendr-aggregated anonymised contracts show annual deals from ~USD 25,000 (small team, limited module access) up to USD 250,000+ (enterprise, multi-asset-class, with API), with a commonly cited median of ~USD 49,334/yr (range USD 27,674-77,221); costbench.com lists four tiers spanning USD 25,000-80,000+/yr; investables.ai states API/data-feed access typically adds 30-60% on top of the base subscription, implying API-specific spend of roughly USD 15,000-75,000+/yr on top of a base plan. None of these are vendor-published prices.
ml_training_license: Preqin's public Terms & Conditions (https://classic.preqin.com/item/terms-conditions/304) do not explicitly mention AI or ML training. The licence is non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, restricted to lawful purposes and internal business use, and separately prohibits automated/robotic ('web crawler') access, copying/duplication, redistribution and commercial exploitation of the Service or Data. Unknown whether internal ML training is permitted — Inference: this would very likely require written clarification or a negotiated rider, since bulk API pulls feeding a training pipeline could be read as exceeding the 'specified purposes'.
language: English (core platform and data records); some marketing material exists in other languages, but the underlying deal and fund records are English.
update_frequency: Feeds API: daily sync. Underlying platform data continuously updated by Preqin research teams.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Good for sponsor-side signals — fundraising cycles, GP/LP behaviour, PE/VC deal and exit records — that correlate with M&A activity, and the Feeds API is a genuine bulk CSV channel. But the universe centres on funds, GPs, LPs and deals rather than an exhaustive private-company registry, so it is a partial source that would need pairing with a company-level dataset. Also above the stated budget.

name: CB Insights
data_types: Private and public company profiles; funding/investment transactions; cap-table history; M&A and IPO exit data; business-relationship data (partnerships, M&A-relevant signals); proprietary predictive scores including the Mosaic Overall Health Score and an Exit Probability score split into IPO and M&A likelihood, plus Momentum/Money/Market/Management sub-scores; technology market maps; expert research and newsletters.
coverage_geo: 12M+ company profiles claimed, described as worldwide. No specific Asia or Japan company count was found in public materials.
history_depth: Company founded 2008; first platform version launched February 2010; roughly 15+ years of tracked funding and deal history. Per-record historical depth is not itemised publicly.
api: Yes — REST API v2 (v1 now in maintenance mode), OAuth2 client-credentials auth via https://api.cbinsights.com/v2/authorize; documented endpoints for organizations, financial transactions (investments, M&A, IPOs), business relationships, and predictive scores. Docs: https://api-docs.cbinsights.com/
bulk_delivery: Yes — marketed as 'APIs and data feeds' (https://www.cbinsights.com/what-we-offer/api/), implying bulk feed delivery alongside the API, though no separate public bulk-file specification was found.
pricing: No public list price; a custom quote is required. Third-party estimates only (all labelled third-party estimates, observed 2025-2026): Vendr median USD 46,984/yr (range USD 24,748-184,986); costbench.com four tiers from USD 29,800-100,000/yr; easyvc.ai cites ~USD 50,000-85,000/yr typical and up to ~USD 265,000/yr enterprise; one source cites team plans at USD 4,134-20,416/month billed annually (~USD 50k-245k/yr). None are vendor-published.
ml_training_license: EXPLICITLY PROHIBITED. The CB Insights Master Subscription Agreement (https://www.cbinsights.com/legal) Sec. 1(d)(ii) bars use of Licensed Materials 'in connection with the development of any software program, model, algorithm, or other generative AI tool, including training or teaching any large language model.' Sec. 1(d)(iv) separately bans scraping, mining and automated extraction. Sec. 1(e) commits CB Insights not to use Customer Data to train its own AI. Net effect: standard terms directly forbid the intended use; a bespoke ML rider would have to be negotiated.
language: English
update_frequency: Continuously updated by CB Insights research/data operations; the API is queried live against current data.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Content-wise this is among the strongest fits available — CB Insights already runs an internal M&A/Exit-probability model over structured deal, funding and relationship data, and exposes those scores via API. However its MSA explicitly and specifically prohibits using licensed data to train AI/ML models, making it unusable for the stated purpose without a negotiated exception. A major legal blocker despite the best data fit.

name: AlphaSense
data_types: AI-powered search and analytics over broker research, SEC filings, earnings-call transcripts, news, expert-call transcripts (via Tegus), company financials, and a private-markets/PE database of structured financials for public and private companies; 'GenSearch' generative-AI answer product; Company Financials module.
coverage_geo: Claims 40M+ public and private companies tracked globally. A private-equity database sub-product covers 37,000 public plus 1.4M private companies with structured financials. One source states more than 10M private companies covered across EMEA and Japan specifically — the only explicit Japan coverage claim found in this vendor group, likely a subset of the 40M global figure. No explicit deal/M&A transaction count was found.
history_depth: Company founded 2011; underlying source documents (filings, transcripts, broker research) carry their own multi-year histories, but AlphaSense publishes no aggregate 'years of data' figure.
api: Yes — documented developer platform at https://developer.alpha-sense.com/, including a GraphQL API, a Document/Search REST API, an Ingestion API, an Agent API (GenSearch) and a JavaScript SDK. Auth via API key, client ID + secret, or OAuth-style credentials; default base URL https://api.alpha-sense.com.
bulk_delivery: Partial — the documented Ingestion API implies structured pipeline-style access, but no public bulk full-database file-export product was found; delivery is API/SDK-centric.
pricing: No public list price; sales-negotiated only, no self-serve tier. Third-party estimates only (labelled as such, observed 2026): Vendr median USD 17,500/yr across 38 purchases (range USD 9,250-51,000); SpendHound SMB average ~USD 12,210/yr and enterprise average ~USD 123,760/yr (enterprise reported up ~20% YoY, SMB down ~19% YoY).
ml_training_license: EXPLICITLY PROHIBITED. AlphaSense's Terms of Use (https://alpha-sense.com/terms/) Sec. 2.2(m) bars using the Services or any Content with 'any other platform, software, software solution, or other manual or automatic tools (including ... any third party artificial intelligence or machine learning tool ("AI Tool") or large language model ("LLM") or API'. Sec. 2.2(c) separately bans data mining, scraping and automated extraction. Note: AlphaSense's separate public statements that it does not train its own LLMs on customer data address a different question and are not a grant of rights for the customer to train models on AlphaSense content.
language: English (platform/UI); underlying documents may be in other source languages but the core product is English.
update_frequency: Continuous ingestion of new filings, transcripts, research and news; expert calls published after an embargo period.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Strong for qualitative and expert-opinion signal plus point-in-time company financials, and it is one of the few in this group with an explicit Japan private-company coverage claim. But it is not primarily a structured historical M&A transaction database, and the ToU explicitly ban feeding Content into any AI/ML tool or LLM — a poor fit for the training use case under standard terms.

name: Tegus (acquired by AlphaSense, 2024)
hq_country: United States (Chicago); parent AlphaSense HQ New York. AlphaSense acquired Tegus in 2024 for ~USD 930M.
data_types: Expert call transcripts (35,000+ across TMT, consumer, energy and life sciences); company financial models and KPIs for 4,000+ public companies with fully driveable models; SEC filings and earnings-call transcripts (via the BamSEC acquisition Tegus made in 2021).
coverage_geo: 35,000+ public and private companies in the expert-transcript library, historically weighted toward US-listed and US-focused sectors. AlphaSense has stated plans to 'more than double' the Tegus expert-transcript library's APAC and EMEA coverage, which implies current Asia/Japan depth is comparatively thin. Inference: weak current Japan coverage, improving over time.
history_depth: Tegus founded 2013; the expert-transcript library was built over roughly the past decade. BamSEC-sourced SEC filings and earnings transcripts extend back through each covered company's own filing history (years to decades for large-cap US filers).
api: Yes, historically — vendor material references an Excel add-in and API access for workflow integration. Post-acquisition, Tegus content is delivered through the AlphaSense platform and developer API (https://developer.alpha-sense.com/); no standalone public Tegus API documentation was found post-integration.
bulk_delivery: Unknown / not found publicly. No bulk full-file-dump product was located; the documented delivery paths are the API and the Excel add-in.
pricing: No public list price. Third-party estimate only (observed 2026, aggregator citing Vendr-style data): median ~USD 30,000/yr, range USD 13,000-65,200/yr for a Tegus subscription. Expert calls are billed separately at the expert's hourly fee (~USD 450/hr average, third-party estimate) plus a flat USD 75 transcription fee with no markup, per Tegus's stated model.
ml_training_license: EXPLICITLY PROHIBITED — now governed by AlphaSense's Terms of Use (https://alpha-sense.com/terms/), which bar using Content with any third-party AI/ML tool or LLM (Sec. 2.2(m)) and ban data mining and automated extraction (Sec. 2.2(c)). The same prohibition applies to Tegus content delivered via AlphaSense.
language: English
update_frequency: New expert calls added continuously (published after an embargo period); financial models updated each earnings cycle.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Primarily qualitative expert-opinion content and single-company financial models rather than structured historical M&A transaction records — a poor direct fit for training a target-prediction model. And as with AlphaSense, standard terms explicitly forbid feeding the content into any AI/ML tool.

name: Owler (a Meltwater company)
hq_country: United States (San Mateo, CA); parent Meltwater is Norway/US-based, acquired Owler June 2021
data_types: Acquisition/M&A history (acquirer, target, date, deal amount or 'undisclosed' flag, source), funding rounds, revenue estimates, employee/headcount estimates, executives, ranked competitors, and news/key-event triggers (funding announcements, leadership changes, hiring). No explicit predictive score field was found.
coverage_geo: Owler states over 15 million company profiles, sourced partly from a community of 5 million+ global business professionals plus AI/ML and human data-science verification. No published Asia or Japan coverage figures were found.
history_depth: Unknown — not publicly stated.
api: Yes (REST). Owler's developer portal at developers.owler.com returned almost no public content (mostly gated behind signup). Third-party listings (Apify) describe an underlying Company Intelligence API returning firmographics, competitors, funding, M&A and news. Per UpLead's pricing breakdown, API access (Firmographics, Competitor, News/Key Events APIs) is available only on the Enterprise / 'Owler Max' tier, not on Pro.
bulk_delivery: Unknown / not documented publicly. No bulk file (CSV/Parquet) delivery option was found for Owler.
pricing: Community: free (5 company follows, limited profile views). Pro: USD 39/user/month billed annually (USD 468/user/yr) — UI insights only (revenue estimates, funding, CEO ratings, headcount), no API. Enterprise ('Owler Max'): custom quote only, includes CRM integrations and API access, no public price. Source: uplead.com/owler-pricing (2026), corroborated by the G2 Owler pricing listing.
ml_training_license: Unknown. No public terms addressing AI/ML training were located; Enterprise API terms would need direct negotiation to confirm.
language: English (UI and data labels).
update_frequency: Not precisely stated; the vendor describes continuous AI/ML-assisted updates supplemented by a human data-science team, but publishes no refresh cadence.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Has the right signal categories (funding + M&A + firmographics + news triggers) but API and bulk access sit behind an undisclosed Enterprise price, the data is partly crowd/community-sourced (a quality and consistency risk for ML training), and no Asia/Japan depth is documented. Moderate fit; requires a vendor call to validate API terms, price and coverage before committing budget.

name: Craft.co
data_types: Confirmed via docs: private-company valuations (pre/post-money), funding-round associations, valuation step-up metrics, and sourced/dated financial data points. Craft markets '250+ data points' spanning financial, operational and human-capital metrics, positioned primarily for supply-chain, supplier-risk and third-party-risk monitoring. Explicit acquisition/M&A event fields were NOT confirmed in the documentation reviewed — Inference: likely present given general company-profile depth, but unverified.
coverage_geo: Global company coverage; no publicly stated total company count and no Asia or Japan depth figure was found. Craft's supply-chain-resilience positioning suggests broad but unverified Asia coverage — Inference, unconfirmed.
history_depth: Unknown — not disclosed publicly.
api: Yes — a GraphQL 'Company Data API' with documentation at docs.craft.co (example query by domain returning valuation history with currency-aware fields).
bulk_delivery: Unknown — no bulk or file-delivery format was found in the available documentation.
pricing: Quote only. No public price points, tiers or amounts were found on Craft's site, G2, Capterra or Vendr. Note: searches surface a distinct 'Craft.io' product-management tool and a 'Craft' docs app, which were excluded as irrelevant.
ml_training_license: Unknown. Craft's general Terms of Service (https://global.craft.co/terms/) prohibit automated scraping and robots without written consent, but no specific clause on using licensed API data for AI/ML training was found.
language: English.
update_frequency: Unknown — not disclosed publicly.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Craft's core product is third-party and supplier risk intelligence, not M&A deal-flow prediction, and acquisition/deal data was not confirmed to exist in its schema. Fit is uncertain without a direct sales conversation — lower priority until M&A-specific fields and pricing are confirmed.

name: Growjo
hq_country: United States (reported as a very small team, ~2 employees per one secondary source — unverified).
data_types: Estimated revenue, growth rate and growth rankings, employee headcount estimates, and some funding information, per secondary-source summaries (Growjo's own /about_our_data page returned HTTP 403 and could not be directly verified). Acquisition/M&A event data was NOT confirmed to exist; Growjo's focus is fast-growing private companies (15-1,000 employees), not deal tracking.
coverage_geo: Global, but focused on small and mid-size private companies and startups (15-1,000 employees). No Asia or Japan coverage figures and no total company count were found.
history_depth: Unknown.
api: Reportedly yes — a 'Database Enrichment API' with 'unlimited API calls' per secondary sources — but no official API documentation URL could be located or verified (the primary about_our_data page returned HTTP 403).
bulk_delivery: Reportedly yes — CSV bulk export is mentioned in secondary-source summaries; format and schema were not verified directly.
pricing: Unverified / secondary-sourced only. However its core strength is startup/funding discovery rather than confirmed acquisition outcome data, Asia/Japan depth is unconfirmed, and real pricing is quote-only with only a third-party estimate (~USD 25k/yr) suggesting it may sit at or above the budget ceiling once the finance/investor add-on is included.
budget_tier: mid ($10k-50k/yr) to enterprise (>$50k/yr) — Inference from an unverified third-party estimate (~USD 25k/yr minimum commitment); Harmonic publishes no price.

name: Coresignal
data_types: Multi-source Company API and bulk data with structured funding_rounds[] and last_funding_round (type, date, amount, currency, investors, num_investors); acquired_by_summary (acquirer, date, price, currency); num_acquisitions_source_[1,2,5] and acquisition_list_source_[1,2,5][] (target company, date, price, currency); IPO fields (is_public, ipo_date, ipo_share_price, stock_ticker, stock_information); plus employee/professional profile data and job postings. Acquisition and funding events are confirmed first-class structured fields in the published data dictionary.
coverage_geo: Global; vendor cites ~70-100M+ company records and 865M+ professional profiles (self-reported, not independently verified). Asia coverage is not separately quantified in the docs found — Inference: likely lighter than US/Europe given LinkedIn- and web-scrape-derived sourcing; unconfirmed.
history_depth: Historical Headcount API provides up to 8 years of monthly headcount and follower time series across 11M+ companies (per coresignal.com/solutions/historical-headcount-api). Funding and acquisition history depth (how far back records go) is not explicitly stated in the docs reviewed.
api: Yes — REST API (Multi-source Company API, Base/Clean Company API, Employee API, Historical Headcount API, Agentic Search API, webhooks). Data dictionaries confirmed directly at docs.coresignal.com.
bulk_delivery: Yes — flat-file datasets (JSONL, Parquet, CSV) organised by country, delivered via S3, Azure or GCS, with daily, weekly, monthly or one-time refresh cadence (per docs.coresignal.com/introduction/delivery-formats).
pricing: Public self-serve API plans (coresignal.com/pricing and docs.coresignal.com, observed September 2026): free trial 2,000 credits/7 days; Mini USD 49/mo (2,500 credits); Starter USD 199/mo (12,000); Pro USD 499/mo (35,000); Growth USD 1,000/mo (150,000); Premium USD 1,500/mo (1,000,000); Scale USD 3,000/mo (4,000,000); Elite USD 5,000/mo (10,000,000). Annual plans carry ~10-20% discount (e.g. Starter USD 2,149/yr, Elite USD 54,000/yr). Company and employee records cost 10-20 credits each; Historical Headcount API calls cost 10 credits each. Bulk flat-file Datasets: 'starts at USD 1,000/month, final price negotiated' — effectively quote-based above that floor.
ml_training_license: Unknown / not explicit. Coresignal markets itself for 'Data for AI' and model-training use cases (coresignal.com/use-cases/data-for-ai), but its public Terms and Conditions state that purchased Data is governed by a separate signed agreement rather than the public T&Cs — so no public document confirms or excludes AI/ML training rights. Must be confirmed in the data purchase contract. Note the marketing positioning is favourable, unlike CB Insights and AlphaSense.
language: English platform and docs; underlying source data (company names, descriptions) is multilingual as scraped from source sites. No explicit Japanese-language field support confirmed.
update_frequency: API data described as near real-time / continuously refreshed; bulk datasets offered on daily, weekly or monthly cadence.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Strong structural fit and the best value-for-money in this research set: funding rounds, acquisitions (both as acquirer and as acquired), IPO status, and up to 8 years of monthly headcount and attrition time series are all present as documented structured fields, directly usable as ML features, with transparent public pricing well inside budget. The main open risks are Asia-Pacific coverage depth and the unresolved AI-training licence question.

name: People Data Labs (PDL)
data_types: Company schema includes structured funding fields: funding_stages[], latest_funding_stage, last_funding_date, number_funding_rounds, total_funding_raised (USD), and funding_details[] (round date, amount, currency, type, investing_companies, investing_individuals). Employee count and growth time series: employee_count_by_month, employee_count_by_month_by_level/by_role, gross_additions_by_month, gross_departures_by_month. Corporate structure: affiliated_profiles (parent/subsidiary flags). Dedicated acquisition/M&A-event and IPO fields were NOT found in the schema section fetched — a gap versus Coresignal.
coverage_geo: Global; PDL markets very large person and company datasets (company dataset cited around 18-74M+ profiles depending on source, self-reported, not independently verified). No Asia-specific coverage breakdown was found — Inference: coverage likely skews to US and English-speaking markets given typical PDL sourcing.
history_depth: Monthly employee-count and growth history is available (employee_count_by_month and related fields) but the exact number of years of backfill was not stated on the schema page fetched. Funding history depth (earliest round captured) is not explicitly stated.
api: Yes — REST API (Company Enrichment API, Company Search API), confirmed via docs.peopledatalabs.com.
bulk_delivery: Yes — full or custom bulk snapshots delivered via S3, Snowflake, Databricks, Azure, GCP or SFTP, in JSON/CSV, with delta files for incremental updates (per docs.peopledatalabs.com/docs/data-license).
pricing: Public pricing (docs.peopledatalabs.com/docs/pricing-detail, observed September 2026): Company Enrichment API — Free plan 100 records/month; Pro monthly tiers USD 0.100/record (350-2,499 records), USD 0.075/record (2,500-4,999), and USD 0.250/record listed for 5,000-8,333 (this tier's rate appears anomalous, possibly a documentation artifact — verify directly before budgeting); Pro annual tiers USD 0.080/record (12,000-119,999), USD 0.060/record (120,000-299,999), USD 0.050/record (300,000-399,999); Enterprise (400,000+/yr) custom-quoted. Company Search API has a parallel tier structure at similar per-record rates. Bulk/full dataset licensing is separately negotiated (quote only).
ml_training_license: Unknown / not explicit from the public pages reviewed. PDL's data-license page states customers may 'use data in any way' during the licence term 'provided they comply with the Acceptable Data Use Policy', but that Policy — which would contain any AI/ML-training-specific restriction — was not directly retrievable. Must be confirmed by reading the Policy in full or contacting PDL.
language: English platform and documentation; no explicit Japanese-language data or field support confirmed.
update_frequency: Not explicitly stated for the API in the pages reviewed; bulk snapshots are refreshed with periodic delta/incremental files.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Good fit for the headcount-growth signal — rich monthly employee_count_by_month/by_level/by_role plus gross additions and departures — and for funding-round history, with transparent per-record pricing. But the schema checked did NOT surface a dedicated acquisition/M&A-event field, a real gap for this specific use case relative to Coresignal, and worth confirming with PDL support before committing budget.

name: Proxycurl (Nubela) — SHUT DOWN July 2025, succeeded by NinjaPear
website: https://nubela.co (Proxycurl itself is discontinued; nubela.co now hosts NinjaPear)
data_types: Proxycurl is confirmed SHUT DOWN as of July 2025 following a January 2025 LinkedIn (Microsoft) lawsuit alleging mass fake-account scraping and resale of LinkedIn profile data; the founder stated that continuing to fight was untenable and wound the product down, directing customers to a successor. The successor, NinjaPear (same company, same domain), explicitly avoids LinkedIn scraping and offers Company Details, Employee Count, Company Funding (history plus investor names), Customer Listing, Competitor Listing, Person Profile, and Company Updates endpoints, sourced from public non-LinkedIn sources. No acquisition/M&A event endpoint was identified.
coverage_geo: Not quantified in the pages reviewed; NinjaPear is a much smaller and newer product than the old Proxycurl and no public coverage-size claims were found. Inference: coverage breadth, especially in Asia, is unverified and likely modest given the 2025 relaunch.
history_depth: Not stated for either funding-history depth or employee-count time series on NinjaPear; Proxycurl's old historical employee-count endpoint is defunct along with the rest of the product.
api: Yes for NinjaPear — a live REST API (confirmed via nubela.co/docs, with Python and JS client libraries on GitHub) including a Company Funding endpoint returning funding history and investor names, and an Employee Count field/endpoint. This is NOT the old Proxycurl API, which no longer exists.
bulk_delivery: No — no bulk-file delivery mechanism was found; NinjaPear appears to be API/credit-call only (pay-as-you-go credits, no S3 or dataset dump product identified).
pricing: Public pricing for NinjaPear (nubela.co/pricing, observed September 2026): 3-day free trial with 10 credits, no card required; a USD 10 starter pack (30-day validity) and larger pay-as-you-go packs (90-day validity); subscription tiers reported at USD 49, USD 299, USD 899 and USD 1,899/month (12-month commitment implied; credits valid 18 months). Per-call costs: Company Details 3 credits/call (up to 6 with extra flags), Company Funding 2 credits/call plus 1 credit per unique investor returned, Employee Count included as a flag on Company Details. Legacy Proxycurl per-credit pricing is no longer live or relevant.
ml_training_license: Unknown — no NinjaPear terms or AUP addressing AI/ML training rights was found. Given the litigation history, any AI-training use of derived data should be treated as legally higher-risk pending explicit written confirmation from Nubela and legal review, since the entire predecessor business was shut down over data-sourcing legality.
language: English platform and docs; no Japanese-language support confirmed.
update_frequency: Not stated in the pages reviewed.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Not recommended as a primary vendor: Proxycurl (the vendor named in the request) no longer exists, and the successor NinjaPear is an unproven, recently relaunched, small product with unverified coverage, no bulk delivery, no confirmed ML-training terms, and a corporate history that includes a shutdown driven directly by a major data-rights lawsuit — a poor legal-risk profile for a durable AI training pipeline.

name: Aylien News API (now Quantexa News Intelligence)
website: https://www.quantexa.com (aylien.com no longer resolves as of September 2026)
data_types: News articles enriched with named entities, categories, sentiment and 'event clustering'. Historically marketed entity-based event/story clustering rather than a strict discrete M&A-event schema.
coverage_geo: Global. A competitor comparison (NewsAPI.ai blog) states Quantexa/QNI covers ~16 languages, narrower than competitors.
history_depth: Unknown / not disclosed post-acquisition. Pre-acquisition Aylien marketed multi-year historical news archives but exact depth was not found in current public materials.
api: Yes — REST API with NER, entity linking/disambiguation, category and sentiment tagging, and event clustering.
bulk_delivery: Not confirmed in current materials; pre-acquisition Aylien supported archive/bulk delivery for enterprise customers. Inference.

Third-party review aggregators (fitgap, TrustRadius, opentools.ai) show legacy Aylien figures — 'starting at USD 29/mo', a free tier (1,000 credits/mo), and a Standard tier at USD 199/mo (50,000 credits) — but the year these applied and whether they are still honoured post-acquisition is unclear; treat as historical (pre-2023 acquisition), not current. Inference: current pricing is enterprise quote-only.
ml_training_license: Unknown. Aylien's own ToS page could not be fetched (domain no longer resolves). A secondary summary of that ToS describes a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable licence for personal/internal business use, prohibiting resale, redistribution, publishing retrieved data and reverse engineering — but does not explicitly address model training. No current Quantexa QNI clause on AI/ML training was found.
language: ~16 languages per a competitor comparison; Japanese-specific coverage was not confirmed in any source consulted.
update_frequency: Historically near-real-time; not reconfirmed for the current QNI product.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Weak fit as currently understood: the product is now enterprise-gated under Quantexa, self-serve access is unclear, the event taxonomy is entity/category/sentiment-based rather than a clear discrete M&A-event schema, and Japanese coverage is unconfirmed. Inference.

name: Event Registry (NewsAPI.ai)
data_types: News articles plus structured, AI-detected 'events' (story clusters of related articles), with named-entity recognition, entity linking and disambiguation, sentiment, semantic annotation and text classification. A dedicated event-search endpoint exists, distinct from plain article search.
coverage_geo: Global — 150,000+ news sources, 60+ languages claimed.
history_depth: Historical article and event data back to 2014 (confirmed on the newsapi.ai/plans pricing page: free tier historical data 'Since 2014') — roughly 12 years.
api: Yes — REST API, plus official Python and Node.js SDKs; a separate event-search endpoint distinct from article search.
bulk_delivery: Not explicitly advertised as bulk file archives; access appears to be purely API/token-based (article search, historical article search, event search, text-analytics endpoints). No dedicated archive-file product was found.
pricing: Public self-serve pricing confirmed at https://newsapi.ai/plans (observed September 2026): Free plan USD 0/mo with 2,000 tokens, current data (last 30 days) and historical data since 2014; paid '5K' plan USD 90/mo with 5,000 tokens. Token costs: article search (recent) 1 token; article search (historical) 5 tokens per searched year; event search (recent) 5 tokens; event search (historical) 20 tokens per searched year. Higher tiers (10K, 20K etc.) exist but their prices were not shown on the page fetched; custom/enterprise pricing available beyond that.
ml_training_license: Unknown — a readable ToS page for newsapi.ai/eventregistry.org could not be retrieved in this session (the page returned a JS-disabled placeholder). No explicit ML-training clause was found.
language: 60+ languages. Japanese (ISO code 'jpn') is explicitly confirmed as supported per the EventRegistry event-registry-python GitHub wiki 'Supported languages' page — one of the few confirmed Japanese-capable news-event sources in this set.
update_frequency: Real-time / continuous ingestion (implied by the 'current data — last 30 days' tier and event-clustering-on-ingest architecture).
fit_for_lead_prediction: Best fit of the news-event group for this use case: a token-metered event-search endpoint distinct from article search, entity linking and disambiguation, confirmed Japanese-language coverage, public low-cost entry pricing, and 12 years of historical event access (with a per-year token surcharge on historical event queries). Whether its taxonomy breaks out 'acquisition/merger' as a discrete category, rather than generic story clustering, was not independently confirmed — verify via a trial account. Inference on taxonomy granularity.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) at entry tiers; likely mid ($10k-50k/yr) for the volumes needed to pull years of historical event data for training, given the per-historical-year token multiplier.

name: Bloomberg Second Measure
data_types: Anonymised and aggregated US consumer credit and debit card transaction panel data (a consumer spend index). NOT news/event data and NOT an M&A deal or event feed.
coverage_geo: Primarily US consumer spending; covers 3,000+ public and private companies and 4,000+ brands per Bloomberg materials. No Asia/Japan relevance.
history_depth: 7+ years of consumer spend history cited in Bloomberg materials.
api: Delivered via Bloomberg Terminal (ALTD, ECAN functions) and separate aggregated/transaction-level data feeds; not a general-purpose public REST API for arbitrary third-party integration.
bulk_delivery: Yes, via Bloomberg data feeds (daily delivery, ~3-day lag), but bundled with Bloomberg's enterprise data distribution rather than sold as a standalone bulk file product.
pricing: No public self-serve pricing; requires a Bloomberg Terminal subscription and/or an enterprise data licence. Bloomberg enterprise data products are not publicly priced.
ml_training_license: Unknown — not researched in depth given the poor fit. Inference: Bloomberg enterprise data licences typically carry strict redistribution and use-case restrictions requiring case-by-case negotiation.
language: English (US-centric consumer data; not a news-language product).
update_frequency: Daily, with a ~3-day lag.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Poor fit — this is consumer transaction and spend data, not M&A news or deal-event data, and it is US-focused, so it is not useful for detecting or predicting M&A targets or for Japanese-market signal. Confirmed via brief research as instructed.

name: RavenPack (incl. Bigdata.com)
data_types: News analytics with a proprietary event taxonomy (RavenPack Analytics / RPA) covering 6,000+ event topics and subtypes, including an explicit 'Mergers & Acquisitions' event category; sentiment scoring; and, in the newer Edge/Bigdata.com product, transcripts and broader unstructured-data coverage. Entity resolution across 300,000+ named entities historically, 12M+ in the newer Edge product.
coverage_geo: Global — 40,000+ sources. Notably, a June 2026 partnership announcement describes RavenPack expanding Japan coverage via JPX (Japan Exchange Group) Market Innovation & Research (JPXI)'s SCRIPTS Asia team, supplying Japanese corporate and investor-meeting disclosures and earnings-call transcripts (Japanese plus professional English translation) through Bigdata.com APIs.
history_depth: The History API offers a full historical archive back to 2000 through the prior month — 20+ years, the deepest archive in this research set.
api: Yes — REST API (RavenPack / Bigdata.com API, plus an R package and other SDKs), and a real-time research-assistant/chat interface on Bigdata.com.
bulk_delivery: Yes — historical archive delivery for backtesting and model training is a core RavenPack product, used heavily in quant finance for exactly this kind of historical event-driven model training.
pricing: No public pricing found. RavenPack does not publish price lists; access is via direct sales negotiation or via data-vendor intermediaries (e.g. WRDS for academic access, which has its own separate fee structure not representative of commercial pricing).
ml_training_license: Unknown, likely restrictive — not confirmed in this session. Inference: RavenPack's per-seat/per-use enterprise financial data licensing model typically requires an explicit ML-training rights clause to be negotiated; assume training use is NOT included by default. That said, RavenPack's archive product is explicitly sold for quant backtesting and model development, so a training rider is plausibly obtainable.
language: Primarily English-language source coverage historically; Japanese-language coverage is newly emerging via the 2026 JPXI/SCRIPTS Asia partnership (transcripts in Japanese plus English translation), not yet a mature core offering.
update_frequency: Real-time news analytics with same-day/next-day event feed, plus the historical archive updated through the prior month.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Strong taxonomy fit — an explicit M&A event category, a 20+ year archive, a large entity-resolution graph, and archive delivery designed for model training. But almost certainly enterprise-priced well above the USD 50k/yr budget, and Japanese coverage is nascent. Inference on pricing tier given no public numbers and RavenPack's positioning with major quant funds and banks.

name: Accern (acquired by Wand AI, February 2025)
hq_country: United States (now operating under Wand AI, HQ Tel Aviv, Israel)
data_types: A no-code NLP/AI platform for financial-text analytics: 1,000+ event distinctions via a proprietary dictionary mapping 30,000+ financial-event-phrase variations to standardised event categories; includes an 'event_impact_score_on_entities' output, with the documentation example given for a 'Mergers & Acquisition' event type against a named entity.
coverage_geo: US-focused — the entity dictionary maps 150,000+ company-name variations to ~8,000 US public equities, with Bloomberg Open Symbology integration (entity_id/global_id). No international entity-resolution coverage is documented.
history_depth: The API itself exposes only a 30-day rolling window. A separate historical archive was offered via FTP/Dropbox delivery covering 2012-08-25 to 2016-08-19 (~4 years, 15M+ articles); no evidence of a maintained archive beyond 2016 was found in the documentation reviewed.
api: Yes — REST API with token auth, JSON/CSV output, ~40ms claimed processing latency per article.
bulk_delivery: Yes historically, via FTP/Dropbox for the archive noted above; the current post-acquisition bulk offering is unclear.
pricing: Historical public pricing found via aggregators: a starting price cited at USD 7,500/feature/month; AWS Marketplace listed a 'Basic' package at USD 3,000/month for 100k units, plus a free trial (50k units, 1 user, Global News). Current post-acquisition pricing is not confirmed — Accern was acquired by Wand AI in February 2025 and by April 2026 reportedly operated with only ~21 employees, suggesting the standalone product and pricing may be in transition. Treat these figures as historical and uncertain for 2026.
ml_training_license: Unknown — no terms or licensing language on ML-training use was found in the documentation reviewed.
language: Not addressed in the documentation reviewed; sourcing is described only as '300 million+ sources' globally with no language breakdown, and entity resolution is explicitly US-equity-only, so Japanese coverage is unconfirmed and likely absent or very limited. Inference.
update_frequency: Real-time ingestion claimed (~40ms/article), with a 30-day rolling API window.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Weak fit: entity resolution and the archive are US-equity-centric, Japanese coverage is unconfirmed and unlikely, the historical bulk archive runs only through 2016 and may no longer be offered, and the company's ownership and product status have been in flux since the 2025 acquisition.
budget_tier: mid ($10k-50k/yr) based on the historical AWS Marketplace 'Basic' tier (USD 3,000/mo ≈ USD 36k/yr); could reach enterprise depending on feature and unit volume.

update_frequency: Unknown, not specified in public materials.

But it is built for VC-backed startups specifically, not the general SME M&A targets typical of a Japanese advisory firm's pipeline (largely unlisted, non-VC-backed SMEs). Inference: likely a poor match for JCAI's actual target universe without heavy adaptation.

name: Dealroom.co (API / Dealroom Signal)
data_types: Company, founder, investor and funding-round data across 100+ fields; 'Dealroom Signal', a momentum score flagging startups likely to raise their next funding round; entity-linked news and sentiment; 'predictive signals'; and stealth-startup detection surfacing companies months ahead of public announcement.
coverage_geo: Global, with strong European startup-ecosystem coverage. Asia coverage is present but not quantified in the sources consulted. Inference: weighted toward Europe and the US given Dealroom's known market focus. Scale: 3M+ companies, 336,000+ funding rounds, 18M+ founder profiles.
history_depth: Funding-round tracking since 2018 (~8 years).
api: Yes — REST API with OAuth2, filterable across 100+ fields; also offers a hosted MCP server for natural-language queries via Claude or Cursor.

language: Not specified; the platform UI is English.
update_frequency: Described as real-time for funding data; the broader dataset refresh cadence is not specified.

Inference: moderate fit at best, mainly useful as training data on company growth trajectory rather than as a ready-made acquisition-propensity score. Bulk Snowflake delivery is a plus.

name: Crunchbase (Predictions & Insights API / Crunchbase Business)

Vendr reports median actual spend of ~USD 20,000/yr with ~21% average discount off list. update_frequency: Continuous/frequent (30M+ updates per year cited); Heat and Growth scores are described as based on recent activity, implying frequent recalculation.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Among the best conceptual fits found: an explicit acquisition-event prediction model (73% stated accuracy) that is API-accessible via the Predictions and Insights package, ~19 years of history, and a plausible mid-tier budget fit at ~USD 20k/yr median spend. Japan and Asia private-company depth is the main uncertainty, along with the training-rights question.

name: SPEEDA (Uzabase, Inc.)
data_types: Industry and company research platform including a database of 1.9M+ M&A deal records searchable by multiple criteria; financial statements, valuation multiples, and company comparison/benchmarking tools. No explicit acquisition-propensity score was found — it is primarily a deal and company research/screening tool.
coverage_geo: Asia-focused with strong Japan coverage, plus global company data; explicitly markets Japan and APAC M&A deal history. This is the strongest Asia deal-history coverage identified in this research set.
history_depth: Not specified numerically in the sources; the M&A database is described as covering historical deals extensively (1.9M+ records).
api: Yes, but reportedly limited to the Enterprise tier (per third-party comparison sites digi-mado.jp and crexgroup.com); allows integration with Salesforce and internal generative-AI systems — notable, since it implies Uzabase contemplates customer AI use.
bulk_delivery: Not clearly documented publicly; likely negotiable at the Enterprise tier.
pricing: Partially public via third-party comparison sites, NOT vendor-confirmed: Basic ~JPY 55,000/month (~USD 370/mo), Professional ~JPY 110,000/month (~USD 740/mo), Enterprise (including API) custom quote. A 14-day free trial with no setup fee is reported. Sources: digi-mado.jp/products/45877, crexgroup.com (year observed 2025-2026; exact vendor confirmation not obtained).
ml_training_license: Unknown — not addressed in any source consulted. The stated support for integration with internal generative-AI systems is a favourable signal but is not a training-rights grant.
language: Japanese (primary); some English-language service pages exist.
update_frequency: Not specified.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Moderate-to-strong fit and arguably the highest-priority vendor conversation for a Japan-focused firm: very strong Japan/Asia M&A deal history and company financials as training features, with an Enterprise-tier API that explicitly contemplates internal generative-AI integration. But there is no vendor-confirmed propensity score, so it would serve as a raw feature and label source rather than a ready-made prediction product.
budget_tier: mid ($10k-50k/yr) — Inference: the Professional-tier monthly figure annualises to roughly USD 8,900/yr, with the unpriced Enterprise/API tier likely pushing above USD 10k.

name: Teikoku Databank (TDB) — Corporate Credit Research / COSMOS2 / COSMOSNET API, plus the annual Successor Vacancy Rate survey
data_types: Company credit scores (0-100 TDB rating), management and leadership profiles, up to 6 years of financials, supplier/customer relationships, and banking relationships. Separately, TDB publishes an annual 'Successor Vacancy Rate' (後継者不在率) study covering ~270,000 Japanese companies — a directly field-researched proxy for business-owner succession risk and propensity to sell, though it is delivered as an aggregate report/PDF rather than a per-company licensable score in the sources found.
coverage_geo: Japan (all 47 prefectures, 83 branch offices, field investigators), plus 100+ countries via a partner network for overseas coverage. Unmatched Japan SME depth.
history_depth: 100+ years of accumulated proprietary company data; reports include up to 1 year of adverse credit history and up to 6 years of financials. The annual succession survey series runs yearly (most recent found: November 2025 edition covering 2025 data).
api: Yes — a COSMOSNET API exists for querying the COSMOS2 company database directly from customer systems. An explicit succession-risk API field was not confirmed in the sources.
bulk_delivery: A data-linkage/integration service (データ連携サービス) exists — e.g. a Salesforce AppExchange listing and an SAP integration with BASF Japan — but bulk pricing is not public.
pricing: Quote only — no public price points were found for CCR reports, the COSMOS2/COSMOSNET API, or the succession-risk survey data. Year observed: 2026.
ml_training_license: Unlikely to be permitted without explicit negotiation. TDB report terms state that reports are confidential and proprietary, with copyright fully reserved and reproduction or translation to third parties prohibited (per the tdb-en.jp CCR page). Inference: bulk ML-training use would require a separately negotiated data licence, not covered by standard report terms.
language: Japanese (primary); English service pages available at tdb-en.jp.
update_frequency: Field investigators conduct ongoing visit-based updates; the succession survey is published annually.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Highest conceptual relevance in the entire set for a Japan-focused predictor: the Successor Vacancy Rate data is essentially the exact 'propensity to sell / exit' signal the firm wants, and TDB's century of SME data covers the ~99% of Japanese companies that are unlisted — unmatched depth for training a Japan M&A model. Inference: the succession data appears to be published as an aggregate report rather than a licensable per-company field, so direct vendor confirmation is needed on whether per-company succession-risk flags can be licensed via API or bulk feed. This is the single most important vendor conversation to have.

name: Tokyo Shoko Research (TSR) — TSR API連携サービス (Company Data API)
data_types: Company basic information (name, address, phone), detailed attributes (revenue, profit, TSR credit score), full financial statements (B/S, P/L), and a statistically derived bankruptcy-probability risk score (1-100 scale, 12-month horizon) — a downside-risk signal rather than an acquisition-propensity signal. Also offers 'TSR REPORT' detailed company dossiers and a sales-lead bulk file product (営業支援ファイル).
coverage_geo: Japan — 10M+ companies in the database, described as one of Japan's largest private-company datasets.
history_depth: Not specified numerically in the sources. Unknown.
api: Yes — TSR provides an API specification and credentials for customers to build their own integration, with a free test environment (XML/PDF retrieval) available during development.
bulk_delivery: Yes — the TSR営業支援ファイル (sales support bulk file) uses a tiered base fee plus per-record fee structure; the per-record cost is reported as low as ~JPY 23 per company at volume.
pricing: Partially public. Bulk file: ~JPY 23/company at scale, per third-party sourcing guides. Single credit reports: JPY 8,000-25,000 (~USD 53-167) each. API integration pricing is quote-only and varies by development scope. Year observed: 2026.
ml_training_license: Unknown — not addressed on the API service page or in other sources consulted.
language: Japanese
update_frequency: Not specified in the sources. Unknown.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Moderate but practically attractive fit. The bankruptcy-risk score is the inverse of what is wanted (distress rather than acquisition propensity), but the underlying 10M+ company financial and attribute dataset at ~JPY 23/record bulk pricing makes TSR a strong candidate as the Japan-wide feature backbone for a custom propensity model, rather than a source of a pre-built acquisition score. The per-record economics are by far the most budget-friendly route to comprehensive Japanese SME coverage found in this research.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) for the bulk file at modest volumes based on the ~JPY 23/record figure; scales into mid tier depending on record count and API development scope.

name: Nikkei Value Search (Nikkei, Inc.)
data_types: Company financial and quantitative data (basic information, major shareholders, macro and industry statistics) plus qualitative data (news articles, corporate activity information, research reports); used for building M&A long-lists and short-lists and for peer/industry analysis. A research and screening tool, not a dedicated propensity-score product.
coverage_geo: Japan-focused: 4,300 listed domestic companies, ~1M unlisted Japanese companies including startups, plus 44,000 global listed companies.
history_depth: Not specified numerically in the sources. Unknown.
api: Yes, an API is available (details require direct inquiry); also integrates with Salesforce and other sales-support systems.
bulk_delivery: Data export in xls/csv/ppt formats is confirmed; true bulk or API delivery terms require direct vendor inquiry.
pricing: Quote only — annual contract billed monthly, no spot contracts; no public price points found. Year observed: 2026.
ml_training_license: Unknown — no AI/ML training terms were found on the public pricing page; requires direct inquiry. Inference: Nikkei is a news publisher and is likely to be restrictive about training use of its editorial content specifically.
language: Japanese (primary)
update_frequency: Not specified in the sources. Unknown.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Moderate fit — a strong Japan private-company universe (~1M unlisted companies) usable as feature and training data for long-list generation, plus Japanese-language news signal and an existing Salesforce integration path relevant to JCAI's stack. But there is no evidence of a built-in predictive acquisition-likelihood score; it functions as a screening and research database.
